promotionGate.reason: Sources establish control anchors and frontier activity, but not authoritative 1326 polygon boundaries.

anchors.label: Kandıra
anchors.evidence: TDV Akça Koca states that Kandıra and its vicinity were taken around 1326.

anchors.label: Aydos
anchors.evidence: TDV Akça Koca states that Aydos was taken by Akça Koca together with Konuralp and Gazi Abdurrahman around the same campaign sequence.

anchors.label: Samandıra
anchors.evidence: TDV Akça Koca states that Samandıra fortress was taken after Aydos and that the Samandıra area was granted to Akça Koca as mülk.

anchors.label: Diapolis / Akçakoca
anchors.evidence: Recent academic material reports Diapolis as taken in 1319; chronology varies in secondary/local literature, so retain source-level date rather than over-normalizing.

anchors.label: Prusias ad Hypium / Konuralp
anchors.evidence: TDV Düzce gives 1321 or 1323 as the conquest date by Konuralp.

anchors.label: Dakibyza / Eskihisar
anchors.evidence: The fortress controlled the İzmit-Istanbul road and Gulf crossing; sources describe repeated changes of control in the broader coastal belt and later Ottoman consolidation. Do not promote it to a clean 1326 Ottoman polygon without date-specific evidence.

anchors.label: Şile
anchors.evidence: TDV material dates Ottoman conquest of Şile to the 1390s; this strongly argues against back-projecting a late Ottoman Şile polygon into 1326.

networkFindings: The northern Bithynian frontier is better represented as a chain of fortified/control anchors and raid corridors than as a single smooth border.
Aydos and Samandıra are especially important because their 1326-era Ottoman control is explicitly tied to Akça Koca's frontier command.
The Black Sea coastal belt should not be globally promoted from later Genoese-presence lists: source chronology must be attached to each node.
The İzmit-Istanbul road and Gulf crossing remain strategically important independent of later administrative boundaries.

notes: Historical control is separated from settlement, fortress, route, and later administrative geography.
Modern district boundaries are not used as 1326 political geometry.
The file is evidence-only and must not be treated as canonical political authority.
